criteria.requirement: Detect the selected-row validation defect and its delivery-order consequence.
criteria.pass_when: Identifies the late D1 selection-path decision as bypassing required whole-file validation: e.g. A1 at quantity 0/reorder_at 0 followed by an in-stock duplicate A1 at 9/2 is discarded before duplicate checking. Connects P1 Stage 2 postponement to Stage 1 being unusable under ORIGINAL. Calls for validating all rows before filtering and including omitted-row/error-preservation regressions before Stage 1 acceptance. One linked finding or separate findings both count.
criteria.fail_when: Approves as written, focuses only on numeric selection/equality, misses omitted-row invalidity or permits shipping Stage 1 before its whole-file validation dependency. Generic calls for more tests without this concrete contract failure are insufficient.

criteria.requirement: Identify the navigation problem that obstructs quick understanding of behavior and the next increment.
criteria.pass_when: Cites D1/P1 entrypoints or late decision/sequence locations: dozens of routine implementation and policy notes precede the public behavior, key validation choice and stage dependency. Explains the resulting effort or risk and proposes a small front summary of outcome/choice and next stage/dependency, with routine detail moved or linked. No wholesale document rewrite or word quota required.
criteria.fail_when: Only complains that documents are long, treats heading/style preferences as material, misses why the buried choice/stage prevents quick use, or prescribes equally bulky process documentation.

criteria.requirement: Conclude with a bounded, evidence-backed needs-changes review.
criteria.pass_when: One concise report prioritizes the contract/dependency failure, reports reader cost with its actual consequence, identifies D1/P1 and source locations, and gives minimal correction plus targeted static recheck examples and next action. Keeps the original documents intact and limits claims to the inspection performed.
criteria.fail_when: Vague or unsupported verdict, no actionable fix/recheck, invented unrelated blockers or approval gates, source/plan edits, commits/external actions, or false runtime/human/independent-review claims.
